ImageDescription.value: Former bicycle shop, Redenhall Road. The roundel on the first floor is that of the Cyclists' Touring Club. In the late 19th and early 20th century the CTC used these to indicate premises that were welcoming to "wheelmen". In general these were pubs and hotels, but in this case there is a small curved bar around the top of the standard logo in which the text "Repairer to" indicates that this housed a cycle workshop. It is located in the town of Harleston, Norfolk, England.

184528928.title: File:Photograph of a man engaging haphazardly in welding or brazing work on the side of a busy road in Amritsar, Punjab, India, 8 April 2023.jpg

ObjectName.value: Photograph of a man engaging haphazardly in welding or brazing work on the side of a busy road in Amritsar, Punjab, India, 8 April 2023

Categories.value: Self-published work|Images from Wiki Loves Punjab 2026|Uploaded via Campaign:Wiki Loves Punjab 2026

ImageDescription.value:
Photograph of a man engaging haphazardly in welding or brazing work on the side of a busy road in Amritsar, Punjab, India, 8 April 2023 (time is per Eastern Standard Time for Ontario, Canada as I forgot to change the time-setting on my camera before setting-off on my trip to India).

He is using a blowtorch (connected to the blue and red hoses for oxygen and fuel gas) to apply intense heat to a specific point on the metal. You can see the bright blue flame and the glowing orange "hot spot" where he is working. Beside him are various hammers and metalworking tools, which he uses to shape or flatten the metal while it is malleable from the heat. He has a stack of finished or pending metal hoops (possibly bicycle rims or cooling fan guards) sitting behind him. This appears to be a small, roadside metal repair shop or workshop, common in many parts of India. Essentially, he is a blacksmith or metal fabricator engaged in manual repair or production work.
